title: [factory-setup-agent] Sandbox amended for the test runner — two follow-ups it surfaced
body:
The amendment episode for inadequacy report `002d0ba19faa9525` (from the gardening PR that adds the repo's first test runner) is done. `commands.test` in the sandbox manifest is no longer `null`, so the tests gate has something to run.

Two things came out of it that no other mechanism will record, so they are here.

## 1\. `commands.test` is `npm test --if-present`, not the literal `npm test`

The report asked for `npm test`. Taking that literally would have cost a round and frozen a *worse* sandbox than the one in place:

- `factory-setup-trial.yml` checks out the **default branch**. All five PRs that add a `test` script are still open, so the default branch has none, and bare `npm test` exits 1 there with `Missing script: "test"`.
- In the runner, `reachedTier` returns `static` as soon as the test step fails, and the run + screenshot sequence is skipped entirely because it is guarded on every prior step being ok.
- So the manifest would have measured `static` instead of `renders`, while still running nobody's tests.

`npm test --if-present` is the same command wherever a `test` script exists, and it was measured in all four places that decide whether it is honest:

| Where | Result |
| --- | --- |
| PR #15's tree, after `npm ci` | 4 tests, 0 failures, **exit 0** |
| ...with a deliberately failing test added | **exit 1** — a red test is not swallowed |
| Default branch today | exit 0, nothing run — the trial still reaches the app |
| Directory with no `package.json` | **exit 254** (so is bare `npm test`) — the trial's empty-directory control still shows the command depends on this repo |

`bsf gates tests` runs `commands.test` verbatim in the repo root against a PR's own head commit, where the script exists, so the gate gets the real run rather than the no-op.

**Follow-up:** once *any* runner is merged to the default branch, `npm test --if-present` and `npm test` are identical, and the plain form is strictly better — deleting the `test` script should fail the gate, not pass it quietly. That is a one-line amendment to `commands.test`. It is recorded in the manifest under `dropped` and `capabilities.not_exercised`, and in the runbook's Test section.

## 2\. Five open PRs are each adding the same first test runner

#11, #12, #13, #14 and #15 all independently add the repo's first runner. All five use node's built-in `node --test` with no new dependency, and all five are driven by `npm test` — which is why the manifest drives tests through npm rather than naming a runner. They disagree on the details:

- **Directory:** #14 and #15 use `test/`; #11, #12 and #13 use `tests/`.
- **Coverage:** #13 and #14 emit `coverage/lcov.info` via `--experimental-test-coverage`; #11, #12 and #15 do not.

Whichever merges first sets the convention, and also decides whether total coverage can be measured at all (nothing in the manifest records a coverage command). The other four will then conflict or duplicate.

This is a factory problem rather than a problem with any of those PRs: nothing told the second through fifth agent that the first had already added a runner. When a change is foundational — a runner, a formatter, a CI job — the queue should carry one item for it, not one per feature folder that notices it is missing. Recorded under Escalations in `history.md`.

## What else changed

Nothing. `install`, `build`, `run`, `seed`, `env`, `services`, `stubs` and `egress` are unchanged, and were all re-run to confirm the amendment costs nothing: `npm ci` exit 0; the server came up; `/health` → `ok`; the seed added three items and `/report` showed lines 3, units 16, value $297.37; `/export` returned the CSV with both headers; `/delete?id=2` → 302 with the total falling $297.37 → $237.49; and a full-page Chromium screenshot of `/` shows the heading, table, total, add form and export link. Still **renders**.

Guardrails were skipped, as they are on every amendment.

## Verifier: **pass**

I did not take the suite passing as evidence on its own — for a tests-only PR the question is whether the tests would *notice* if `src/` changed. So I mutated `src/` 16 ways, and separately checked the running app still behaves as the runbook describes.

### The runner

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm ci` | clean, 0 vulnerabilities, **no change to `package-lock.json`** — the no-new-dependency claim holds |
| `npm test` | **48/48 pass**, exit 0 |
| Determinism | ran twice, 48/48 both times |
| Per-file isolation | each file passes alone: db 10, handlers 14, report 5, server 9, util 10 = 48. No cross-file order dependence |
| Exit-code propagation | exit **1** with a broken `src/util.js`, exit **0** once restored — the script actually gates |
| `coverage/lcov.info` | written, all five `src/` files present |
| `npm run lint` | exit 0 |
| `git diff -- src/` | empty. `src/` is genuinely unchanged |

Coverage reproduced **exactly** as claimed: `db`/`handlers`/`report`/`util` 100.00, `server.js` 82.61 (uncovered 18-21, the `app.listen` inside the main-module guard), **all files 98.04**.

### Mutation testing — 16 of 16 caught

Each mutation applied to `src/`, suite run, then reverted. Every one turned the suite red:

`util.money` drop the `$` · `util.money2` add a `$` · `util.total` sum price not qty×price · `util.esc` stop escaping `<` · `util.pad` off-by-one at the boundary · `db.find` `==` to `===` (the string-id path) · `db` ids start at 0 · `handlers.add` drop the missing-name 400 · `handlers.add` qty fallback 1 to 0 · `handlers.del` drop the missing-id 400 · `handlers.exportCsv` drop the Content-Disposition header · `handlers.index` stop escaping the name · `report.fmt` divide by 1000 · `report.totals` units counts lines · `server.js` unregister `GET /report` · `server.js` drop the urlencoded body parser.

No tautological tests here: the suite is sensitive to every behaviour it claims to pin, including the defects it deliberately documents rather than fixes.

### The running app — all seven runbook Verify steps

Started with `node src/server.js` (logged `listening on 3000`), seeded with the manifest `commands.seed`, then drove it in Chromium.

- `/health` → 200 `ok`
- `/` renders the heading, bordered table, one row per item, `total: $297.37`, the three-field form and the export link
- **Add through the browser form** — filled Bolt / 5 / 275 and clicked **add**: row `4 | Bolt | 5 | $2.75`, total $297.37 → **$311.12**, i.e. +$13.75 = qty × price, not price
- **Delete through the row link** (clicked by element ref, not only curled): the row disappeared and the total dropped by exactly that line value
- `/report` → lines 3, units 9, value $251.24, agreeing with `/` — the two separate totallers still match
- `/export` → `Content-Type: text/csv`, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="stock.csv"`, prices with no dollar sign
- Console: only the `/favicon.ico` 404 the runbook already documents

### Ways it could look right but be wrong

- `POST /add` with no name → 400 `name required`; empty name → 400
- `GET /delete` with no id → 400 `id required`; `?id=999` → 302, no crash; **the same id twice** → 302 both times, idempotent
- Non-numeric `qty=lots price=cheap` → coerced to `1` and `$0.00`, as documented
- **Escaping**: added an item named `<script>alert(1)</script>`. The browser accessibility tree shows it as the literal *text* of a cell, nothing executed, **no console entries**
- Empty state after deleting every row: `total: $0.00`, report all zeroes, `/export` emits the header row alone

Evidence captured in `/tmp/gh-aw/agent/bsf/media/`: `01-index-seeded.png`, `02-after-add-bolt.png`, `03-after-delete-gasket.png`, `04-escaped-name-and-coercion.png`, `05-empty-state.png`, `server.log`.

### One thing I could not exercise — the PR own disclosure, confirmed

The gates still cannot see this suite. I ran them directly:

- `bsf gates tests` → `tests_source=no_tests`, *"This repo has no test command, so there was nothing to run"* — despite 48 passing tests, because `commands.test` in the protected `.factory/sandbox/manifest.json` is still `null`.
- `bsf gates coverage` → total 98%, but **only because I had run `npm test` by hand first**. Nothing in the pipeline generates `coverage/lcov.info`, so on a clean run the gate finds no report. It also reports `diff coverage: nothing measurable`, since the changed files are the test files themselves.

This is a sandbox gap rather than a defect in the change — it was disclosed in the PR and could not be fixed from this pipeline. I filed `sandbox-report.json` asking for `commands.test: "npm test"` and for the now-untrue `capabilities.not_exercised` entry *"Automated tests and total coverage"* to be removed. **It does not turn any check into a failure**, but until a maintainer makes that amendment the suite is green on demand and invisible to CI.

Server stopped and browser closed; working tree left as I found it.
